# HTTP and WebSocket contract

With the default `STAT_HTTP_BASE_PATH=/api/v1`, the service exposes:

- `POST /api/v1/stat/session/start`: validates required dimensions, generates a session UUID, and enqueues a `session_start` event; returns HTTP 200.
- `POST /api/v1/stat/events`: processes events sequentially and returns HTTP 202 with the number enqueued when the full request succeeds.
- `GET /api/v1/stat/summary/task/:task_id`: returns one user-scoped task summary or `summary: null`.
- `GET /api/v1/stat/summary/tasks`: returns user-scoped summaries with optional UUID/time filters and normalized pagination (default 20, maximum 200, negative offset becomes zero).
- `GET /api/v1/stat/summary/session/:session_id`: returns a user-scoped active-learning and activity-count projection.
- `GET /ws/v1/stat/events`: accepts `session_start` and `events_batch` messages and returns `session_started` or `events_accepted` acknowledgements.
- `GET /internal/health`: process health only; it does not prove ClickHouse or buffer health.
- `GET /internal/v1/students/:student_id/learning-sessions/:session_id/summary`: exact-token service read of the same bounded session projection; the route is absent when `STAT_INTERNAL_TOKEN` is empty.

All user routes require parseable `X-User-Id` and non-empty `X-User-Role`; `X-Language` is read but unused. The service verifies no bearer token and performs no role checks. The WebSocket upgrade uses these headers and currently accepts every Origin. It has no explicit read limit, deadline, ticket, or subprotocol authentication.

Current requests require `course_id`, `lesson_id`, `task_id`, `platform`, and `editor_mode`. Each batch item requires `session_id` and an allowed `event_type`, may override the root dimensions, and may include arbitrary JSON-object payload. Intervention-relevant events additionally require a stable `event_id`. `course_version_id` is not a current request field despite the legacy database column.

Batch validation and enqueue are sequential. If a later item is invalid or enqueue fails, earlier items can already be accepted even though the HTTP response is an error and does not report the partial count. There is no request-body or batch-count limit configured in the service.
